h: Betzalel Finds the Menorah Within the Shadow of God

p: הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא כא, ב)
this is according to what is written (Yoma 21b):
and the Menorah in the south.
And there it refers to the Menorah of the Mikdash;
and it appears that the lamps
are a semblance of the holiness of the Menorah of the Mikdash.
And in Midrash Rabbah (on this parshah, Bamidbar Rabbah 15:4):
"'Beaten work shall the Menorah be made'
וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן נִתְקַשָּׁה מֹשֶׁה
"and again he had difficulty with it,
and went down and forgot," etc.,
"until He took a coin of fire
and showed him how it is made;
it was difficult for Moshe," etc.,
and he made it at once.
He began to wonder and said:
did the Holy One, blessed be He, show me,
and I had difficulty making it;
and you, who did not see,
made it from your own understanding!
in the shadow of God you were standing
when the Holy One, blessed be He, showed me
did Moshe have difficulty with it,
even though Hashem, may He be blessed, showed him
from his own understanding at once?
"in the shadow of God you were"?
And even if it is only an exposition
on his name, that he was so called,
שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
that the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moshe:
Make Me a Mishkan, an Ark and vessels.
where shall I put them? etc.
Perhaps you were in the shadow of God."
but that you give Me light
as I gave you light," etc.;
To a sighted man and a blind man," etc.;
the Holy One, blessed be He, called Moshe
the light of the Oral Torah;
and this is called "Give Me light";
מַאי קָעָבֵיד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
"What was the Holy One, blessed be He, doing?" etc.
"The Holy One, blessed be He, says pure,
and they said: Who will decide?
and it appears as though they give light,
as it were, to Hashem, may He be blessed.
in truth they are the words of the living God,
what Hashem, may He be blessed, imparts
into the hearts of the Sages;
it appears as though the Sages innovate;
and it is like the parable
of the sighted man and the blind man,
where it appears as though the blind man gives light
and lights the lamp for the sighted man.
וְעֵסֶק שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And the occupation of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
And for this reason it says
at the end of eight rows,
the aspect of the Oral Torah,
and therefore Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
לֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ מָה הוּא אוֹמֵר
did not know what he was saying
Rebbi, from where do you know this?
It is a halachah l'Moshe mi'Sinai.
His mind was set at ease."
he handed to Yisrael only the halachos,
and no one knows their reasons;
they are rather like a law without a reason;
And this is the aspect of
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him.
For the Oral Torah of the Sages
so that it seems to them
that they innovate from their own minds,
of which it is not apparent
with Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
that this too is from Sinai,
explicitly from Hashem, may He be blessed.
And this is the matter of what is written
from Hashem, may He be blessed,
and also the meaning of "Thus says"
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
according to what is written in the holy Zohar
"Koh, which is ready to bless them;
is the aspect of the Shechinah.
Which is not so with Moshe Rabbeinu,
who prophesied with "This is the thing":
it was the word of Hashem
that went out through his mouth,
that it was the word of Hashem.
that they are from Hashem, may He be blessed,
that he did not understand the matter of the Menorah
how is it possible to say this,
to give light to Hashem, as it were?
that he sat at the end of eight rows
Which is not so with Betzalel,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א ב, יט)
And the well was in Miriam's merit
and King David, peace be upon him,
is a chariot for the attribute of Malchus
we call it the Oral Torah;
and David is the head of those with the Divine spirit,
from his own understanding at once.
And about this Moshe said to him,
"In the shadow of God you were":
and it is the attribute of night,
which alludes to the Oral Torah,
And therefore he understood at once
which alludes to "Come and give Me light,"
to give light to Hashem, as it were,

p: And likewise the matter of the Ark,
which alludes to the Torah scholar,
the vessel that receives words of Torah;
from "Inside and outside you shall overlay it":
whose inside is not like his outside
And we find in Midrash Rabbah
and if he has no fear of sin,
he has nothing in his hand.
I have a thousand measures," etc.;
you have nothing in your hand.
If you have fear of sin,
'the fear of Hashem is his treasure.'"
the fear of Hashem is his treasure,"
only about the six orders of the Mishnah.
that he innovated through his reasoning
הָיָה גַּם כֵּן מְפוֹרָשׁ לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו
was also explicit before his eyes
he did not need a Mishkan and a storehouse
in which to place the Ark;
being the aspect of the Oral Torah,
Which is not so with Betzalel,
who was from the root of the Oral Torah
who think that they innovate from their own minds,
for this there is needed first
And the Mishkan is the place of fear:
as written in the holy Zohar
to place the Ark within it;
the vessel that holds words of Torah,
as one learns about the Torah scholar
from the Ark in the Gemara,
And this is what he asked him,
and about this he said to him:
"Perhaps you were in the shadow of God
is the aspect of the Oral Torah,
הוּא שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
is the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He,
for the Holy One, blessed be He,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב ס, א)
for the blessing before Torah study
"When I call the Name of Hashem,
for "the Name of Hashem" is the Torah,
and it is the Written Torah,
which receives from the Written Torah,
And likewise the Written Torah is called the sun,
is the aspect of the moon,
and this is "the shadow of God."
Which is not so with Moshe Rabbeinu,
for whom it was explicit before his eyes
that even the halachos he innovated
in the aspect of the Written Torah
and the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He;
and therefore there was no difference for him
and the Ark and the vessels,
who holds within him words of Torah.
And therefore he did not understand
that a Mishkan would be needed first
in which to put the Ark and vessels,
And likewise he did not understand either
that it be "Come and give Me light,"
which is the aspect of the Oral Torah;
just as he did not understand
תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
the Oral Torah of Rabbi Akiva,
at the end of eight rows
וְלֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ מָה הוּא אוֹמֵר
and did not know what he was saying;
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה חֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
for this was the portion of Rabbi Akiva,
who was the root of the Oral Torah,
מִי יִתֵּן לִי תַּלְמִיד חָכָם וְכוּלֵּי
Who will give me a Torah scholar," etc.;
and it says (Avos d'Rabbi Nasan, chapter 6):
he was standing at the mouth of the well;
אָמַר מִי חָקַק אֶבֶן זֶה וְכוּלֵּי
he said: Who hollowed this stone?" etc.;
one can wear away the heart of stone.
to wear away the heart of stone.
And this is the fiftieth gate,
which was handed over to the penitent.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Which is not so with Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
and the house filled with light (Sotah 12a):
he had no grasp at all
of the matter of the Oral Torah
And it is all one matter.
which corresponds to the attribute of Malchus
in the aspect of the Menorah of the Beis HaMikdash,
that it be "Come and give Me light,"
and there is a flow from the Oral Torah;
is like the Menorah of the Mikdash.
the parshah of the lighting of the Menorah
this is the holiness of this Shabbos,
a flow from the Oral Torah.
